messages:
jerry (Acme): Hey team, since yesterday our Private deployment (VPC) started returning intermittent 403s when talking to Redwood via our corporate proxy. Works sometimes, then fails with CONNECT errors. Using our normal egress allowlist + proxy.

maria (Redwood Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the client-side curl output (with -v) and the proxy response headers if you have them? Also which mode of Private (VPC peering / NAT / proxy) are you using?

jerry (Acme): We're on Private (VPC) with outbound through corp-proxy (explicit HTTP proxy). Quick curl we ran: 
```
$ curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://inference.private.redwood.local/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://inference.private.redwood.local/health
*   Trying 10.1.2.3:8080...
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.1.2.3) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT inference.private.redwood.local:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.private.redwood.local:443
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
>
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Content-Type: text/plain
< Content-Length: 9
< X-Proxy-Phase: inspect
<
Forbidden
* Connection #0 to host corp-proxy left intact
```
No TLS handshake recorded on our side after the CONNECT. Proxy seems to reply 403 immediately.

sanjay (eng-oncall): Hm — interesting header X-Proxy-Phase: inspect. Sounds like an inspection proxy that either blocks CONNECT based on SNI or mutates the ClientHello. Does corp-proxy do TLS interception (MITM) or only tunnelling?

jerry (Acme): They claim they do deep-inspect only for selected destinations. We asked them — they said they rewrite Host headers for HTTP and inject an internal header for logging. They denied MITM for 443.

maria (Redwood Support): Two likely failure modes: 1) Proxy blocks CONNECT when Host header/SNI don't match an allowlist (sometimes proxies compare CONNECT host vs Host header), 2) Proxy injects headers and treats CONNECT as plain HTTP, rejecting because it sees suspicious fields. Can you run a packet capture (tcpdump) from the client for the CONNECT/response? If you can't share pcap, paste the full verbose output with --proxy-header and --trace-ascii.

jerry (Acme): Attached a sanitized tcpdump snippet (paste below). We see the client sending CONNECT, then proxy responds 403 with a short body — no subsequent TLS records. Also found proxy adds an internal header in CONNECT payload? (weird)

lina (eng-infra): Quick repro step you can run locally to emulate: use socat to make a raw CONNECT and see if the proxy echoes any injected lines before the 200/403. Example: 
```
$ printf "CONNECT example.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com:443\r\n\r\n" | nc corp-proxy 8080 -w 3 | sed -n '1,20p'
```
If you get anything other than a clean 200/403 line (e.g., extra headers inserted by the proxy before final response), that's the proxy mutating.

sanjay (eng-oncall): Also ask the proxy team whether they rewrite SNI or strip it. Some enterprise proxies rewrite SNI to a monitoring host or remove SNI and rely on other heuristics — that breaks our client-server TLS if we expect SNI to match the hostname. If their inspector expects to see the Host header and the CONNECT doesn't include it in the canonical form, they might reject.

jerry (Acme): Ran the socat/nc test. Output shows an extra header line before the 403: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Server: BlueGateProxy/3.2
X-Internal-Decision: blocked_inspection
Content-Length: 9

Forbidden
```
So they add X-Internal-Decision. Also noticed when we try sending the CONNECT with IP instead of hostname it returns 200 and then TLS handshake starts — but Redwood cert SNI mismatch then fails TLS.

maria (Redwood Support): That behavior is consistent with proxies enforcing an allowlist on hostname-based CONNECT. If CONNECT by IP is allowed but hostname is blocked (because the proxy can't inspect SNI?), that explains the intermittent success (maybe sometimes route resolves to IP and bypasses the rule) and failures. Two immediate options:
- Have proxy team add inference.private.redwood.local to the CONNECT allowlist / disable inspection for that FQDN.
- Add an egress rule to route traffic to Redwood's Private endpoint outside of the corp-proxy (direct NAT or an explicit bypass for that CIDR).

sanjay (eng-oncall): For a short-term workaround you can also use TCP port tunneling through an approved egress host (bastion) and do TLS over that tunnel. But that's messy. We should also check if your client is sending a Host: header with ":443" which some proxies mis-handle. Try this curl variant: 
```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 --proxy-header "Host: inference.private.redwood.local" https://inference.private.redwood.local/health
```
That forces Host header without port. Some proxies treat Host: with :443 differently.

jerry (Acme): Tried forced Host header — still 403. Pushed the ticket to corp-proxy team and they admitted a policy rule matching on domain suffix that was blocking tunnels for internal vendor endpoints set to "inspect". They changed the rule to allow inference.private.redwood.local as a tunneled destination.

lina (eng-infra): Great. Once they allow CONNECT through, you should see a 200 and then a TLS ClientHello from your client. If TLS handshake fails due to SNI mismatch (because they MITM), we'll need the proxy to either present a cert signed by a corporate CA pinned in your clients, or to not MITM that destination.

jerry (Acme): They allowed the FQDN. Confirmed fix: 
```
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.1.2.3) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT inference.private.redwood.local:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.private.redwood.local
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=inference.private.redwood.local
```
App is healthy again. Thanks for the triage steps — the socat test and asking proxy to allow the FQDN were key.

maria (Redwood Support): Awesome — glad that sorted it. We'll add an internal KB article with the socat/nc repro, the curl variants to try, and recommended corporate proxy rules (allow CONNECT to Redwood private FQDNs or bypass by CIDR). Leaving thread open for a day in case anything else pops up. :tada: 

ops-bot: Incident link created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1183 (auto-tracked)

jerry (Acme): Appreciate the help — marking resolved on our side.
